title: 10 Best AI Agent Builders in 2026
summary: Compare the 10 best AI agent builders in 2026, from enterprise platforms like Concourse to no-code tools like Gumloop and frameworks like LangGraph, by who each is for.
body_markdown:
An AI agent builder is a platform for building and deploying your own AI agents, systems that take a goal and act on it across your tools, rather than buying a point solution that does one fixed task. The category has exploded, and it splits into three very different kinds of product: enterprise platforms built for governed, production rollout; no-code canvases aimed at business users; and developer frameworks for engineers writing agents in code. The right builder depends entirely on who is building and where the agents have to run.


This guide compares the ten best AI agent builders in 2026 across all three groups, with who each is actually for. For the broader category, see our guide to[agentic AI tools](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/agentic-ai-tools) ; for what it takes to run agents at company scale, see[enterprise AI agents](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/enterprise-ai-agents) .


## **What is the best AI agent builder?**


> The best AI agent builder in 2026 depends on who is building: Concourse for enterprises that need production agents with security, integration, and traceability built in; Gumloop, n8n, Lindy, and Relevance AI for no-code building by business teams; Microsoft Copilot Studio and Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for their respective ecosystems; and LangGraph and CrewAI for engineers building in code.


> **Concourse is the enterprise AI agent builder on this list.** Rather than a blank no-code canvas, it is a platform that builds and deploys AI agents into real enterprise workflows, connected to the ERP, data warehouse, and source systems, with the security, governed data access, human-in-the-loop control, and traceability that production work demands. It is built for enterprises that need agents that actually run on their systems, not demos.


## **The three types of AI agent builder**


- **Enterprise platforms** build and deploy production agents with governance, security, and deep system integration: Concourse, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
- **No-code / low-code builders** let business users assemble agents on a visual canvas: Gumloop, n8n, Zapier, Make, Relevance AI, Lindy.
- **Developer frameworks** give engineers full control over agent logic in code: LangGraph, CrewAI.

## **The 10 best AI agent builders in 2026**


### **1. Concourse, Best for Enterprise**


Concourse is an enterprise AI agent builder. Rather than hand you a blank canvas and leave the integration, governance, and reliability to you, it builds and deploys agents directly into real enterprise workflows, connecting to the ERP, data warehouse, billing, and source systems and running the work end to end. Every output traces back to source data and is validated against evals built for your business, which is what lets an agent's work stand up to a board or an auditor.


That is the gap most agent builders leave open: getting from a prototype on a canvas to an agent you can actually trust in production. Concourse is built for that from the start, SOC 2 Type II certified, with governed data access, human-in-the-loop control over consequential actions, and 100+ integrations including NetSuite, QuickBooks, Snowflake, Salesforce, and Stripe. It meets teams where they work, inside ChatGPT, Claude, Slack, Teams, and email, and customers report cutting manual work by roughly 75% and saving 20+ hours per user per month. Its depth is in finance workflows, forecasting, variance analysis, reconciliations, and reporting, which is where enterprise agents have to clear the highest bar for trust.


**Best for.** Enterprises that need production-grade agents with security, deep integration, and audit-ready traceability, not just a builder to prototype in.


**Keep in mind.** Concourse is an enterprise platform with its deepest strength in finance, not a general consumer no-code toy; it is built for teams that need agents to run on real systems and hold up to scrutiny.


### **2. Gumloop, Best for No-Code Business Teams**


Gumloop is a no-code, drag-and-drop canvas for building multi-step AI agents and workflows, pitched at letting non-technical employees build their own automations with IT-controlled access. A Y Combinator (W24) company founded in 2023, it[raised a $50M Series B led by Benchmark in March 2026](https://betakit.com/vancouver-founded-gumloop-sticks-50-million-usd-series-b-round-to-let-employees-build-their-own-ai-agents/) , after a $17M Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners.


**Best for.** Business and ops teams at tech companies that want employees building their own agents on a visual canvas.


**Keep in mind.** No-code canvases are flexible, but design, testing, integration, and maintenance are on you.


### **3. n8n, Best for Technical Teams That Want Control**


n8n is a source-available ("fair-code") workflow-automation platform that has moved hard into AI agents and orchestration, blending no-code nodes with the ability to drop into code, and it can be self-hosted. Founded in 2019 in Berlin, it[raised a $180M Series C led by Accel at a $2.5B valuation in October 2025](https://www.finsmes.com/2025/10/n8n-raises-180m-in-series-c-funding-at-2-5-billion-post-money-valuation.html) , one of the category's headline raises.


**Best for.** Technical teams and self-hosters that want control and the option to extend agents with code.


**Keep in mind.** The flexibility comes with more complexity than a pure business-user tool.


### **4. Microsoft Copilot Studio, Best for Microsoft Shops**


Copilot Studio is Microsoft's low-code/pro-code platform for building and orchestrating agents across Microsoft 365, Teams, and the Power Platform, with a lightweight Agent Builder that reached general availability in 2025. For enterprises standardized on Microsoft, it builds agents right where work already happens. Microsoft is public (NASDAQ: MSFT).


**Best for.** Microsoft-centric enterprises that want governed agents inside their existing tools.


**Keep in mind.** Its value is tied to the Microsoft ecosystem.


### **5. Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Best for Google Cloud**


Google's enterprise agent builder, renamed the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform in 2026 (formerly Vertex AI Agent Builder), is a full-stack platform spanning the code-first Agent Development Kit, a low-code studio, and a managed runtime, with access to Gemini and other models. Alphabet is public (NASDAQ: GOOGL).


**Best for.** Enterprises building agents on Google Cloud.


**Keep in mind.** The branding has shifted recently, so confirm the current product names, and it is at its best inside Google Cloud.


### **6. Relevance AI, Best for Building an AI "Workforce"**


Relevance AI is a no-code platform for building teams of agents, an "AI workforce", via a visual builder, with a text-to-agent "Invent" mode. Founded in 2020 in Sydney, it[raised a $24M Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners in 2025](https://www.smartcompany.com.au/startupsmart/relevance-ai-agent-37-million-series-b-raise/) . It leans into multi-agent systems rather than single agents.


**Best for.** RevOps and business teams that want to build coordinated multi-agent workflows without code.


**Keep in mind.** Multi-agent setups add coordination complexity; start with one agent before orchestrating many.


### **7. Lindy, Best for SMB and Individual Automation**


Lindy is a no-code builder for business-automation agents, email, scheduling, support, CRM, created from natural-language instructions. Founded in 2023 by Flo Crivello, it has raised around $50M from backers including Andreessen Horowitz and Menlo Ventures. It is aimed at individual productivity and SMB operations.


**Best for.** Individuals and small teams automating routine business tasks.


**Keep in mind.** Its sweet spot is SMB and personal automation rather than complex enterprise processes.


### **8. Zapier Agents, Best for the Zapier Ecosystem**


Zapier Agents (formerly Zapier Central) turns Zapier's natural-language AI into "teammates" that act across its thousands of app integrations. For teams already running their operations through Zapier, it is the most natural place to add agents that touch the tools they already connect.


**Best for.** SMB and ops teams already standardized on Zapier.


**Keep in mind.** It is strongest inside the Zapier ecosystem; it is an automation layer, not a deep standalone agent platform.


### **9. LangGraph, Best for Engineers Building Custom Agents**


LangGraph, from the LangChain team, is a developer framework for building stateful, long-running agents in code, with a managed platform for deployment. LangChain[raised a $125M Series B led by IVP at a $1.25B valuation in October 2025](https://dataconomy.com/2025/10/21/langchain-hits-1-25-billion-valuation-in-series-b-led-by-ivp/) . It is the choice when you need full control over agent logic.


**Best for.** Engineering teams building custom agent architectures.


**Keep in mind.** It is code-first, not for business users.


### **10. CrewAI, Best for Multi-Agent Systems in Code**


CrewAI is an open-source Python framework for orchestrating role-based "crews" of agents that collaborate, plus a cloud platform. It[raised $18M from Insight Partners and boldstart ventures](https://www.insightpartners.com/ideas/crewai-scaleup-ai-story/) , with strong developer adoption for building multi-agent systems.


**Best for.** Developers building systems where multiple agents take distinct roles. See our guide to[multi-agent systems](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/multi-agent-systems) .


**Keep in mind.** Like LangGraph, it is for engineers, not business users.


*Also worth knowing:* Make (owned by Celonis) and Stack AI are additional no-code and enterprise options, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides agent infrastructure for AWS teams, and OpenAI's AgentKit includes a visual Agent Builder, though OpenAI has signaled it is winding that specific tool down in favor of its Agents SDK, so check its status before committing.


## **No-code canvas vs. enterprise platform**


The most important choice is not which builder, but which *kind* . A no-code canvas is excellent for the long tail of departmental automations: quick to stand up, owned by the team that uses it. But getting from a prototype on a canvas to an agent you can run in production, on real systems, with data you can trust and outputs you can defend, is a different problem, and it is where most agent projects stall.


> Building a demo agent is easy now; building one that connects securely to your core systems, respects access controls, and produces output you can put in front of an auditor is not. That gap, the last mile to production, is the real work, and it is what an enterprise agent platform exists to close.


That is the distinction between the no-code builders on this list and an enterprise platform like Concourse. For high-stakes, system-of-record work, especially in finance, you want the security, governed integration, and traceability built in rather than bolted on. See our guide to[enterprise AI agents](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/enterprise-ai-agents) for the full set of criteria.


## **How to choose an AI agent builder**


- **For enterprise, production agents on real systems,** choose an enterprise platform with security, integration, and traceability built in, like Concourse, especially for finance and other high-stakes work.
- **For no-code building by business users,** Gumloop, n8n, Lindy, Relevance AI, or Zapier Agents.
- **For agents inside a specific stack,** Microsoft Copilot Studio or the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
- **For engineers who want full control,** a framework like LangGraph or CrewAI.
- **Whatever you choose,** weight security, governed data access, human-in-the-loop control, and traceability, the criteria that separate a demo from production.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is the best AI agent builder?**


It depends on who is building and where the agents run. For enterprise production agents with security and traceability built in, Concourse leads, especially in finance. For no-code building by business users, Gumloop, n8n, Lindy, and Relevance AI; for specific ecosystems, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform; for engineers, frameworks like LangGraph and CrewAI.


### **What is the best enterprise AI agent builder?**


For enterprises, the priority is not the canvas but production readiness: secure, governed access to internal systems, deep integration, human-in-the-loop control, and traceable, auditable output. Concourse is built around exactly those requirements, with particular depth in finance; Microsoft Copilot Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform are strong within their respective ecosystems.


### **What is the best no-code AI agent builder?**


Gumloop, n8n, Zapier Agents, Make, Relevance AI, and Lindy are the leading no-code and low-code builders. Gumloop and Lindy target business users, n8n suits more technical teams, and Relevance AI focuses on multi-agent "workforces." For production agents on core systems, an enterprise platform is usually the better fit than a no-code canvas.


## **The bottom line**


The best AI agent builder depends on who is building: enterprise platforms like Concourse for production agents on real systems, no-code tools like Gumloop and n8n for business and technical teams, ecosystem builders like Copilot Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and frameworks like LangGraph and CrewAI for engineers. The real dividing line is the last mile to production, security, integration, and traceability, which is where enterprise platforms earn their place.
